title: Running the Sixth and Rampart lawn ground and hiring Freddie Keppard's band
summary: With Bab Frank he opened an open-air lawn ground, built a bandstand and hired Freddie Keppard's band, discussing the guitarist, perhaps Brock Mumford.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: That's right. Ice cream company. New Orleans Ice Cream Paula, we called it. Then at that time, I got so popular, I got me a horse and buggy. Well, in those days, that was around about 1910, I was popular. I got a horse and buggy, and had my horse tied out in front of the place, and bought a saloon, even couldn't go in the saloon, and at that time, had a Chinese cook. Well, that went on all right. Then I sold the saloon. I was asked to sell this saloon. Well, I sold it to a fellow. I don't know whether I got any money out of it or not. And then I had a fellow by the name of Bab Frank that played a piccolo in the office. He was selling crabs up and down the street at night with a white coat on and a basket. And he asked me, he said, you're a businessman. He said, I want to talk to you. He said, how would you like to open up a business with me? And I said, what sort of a business? He says, a long ground. Oh, I said, that would be all right. And he was playing with a salsa band from downtown. He played piccolo. And selling crabs in the daytime, see. And so I opened up a business. We opened up a long ground at Sixth and Rampart. It was called the Sixth and Rampart Long Ground. Right back of Plummer's Horseshoe Shop. Had a horseshoe, horseshoe horses in the front. And the back of his place was a long ground. I went to work and put in a platform there. Built a band stand. And my first band that I hired in there was Freddie Kepler.

He got Freddie Kepler. Is that the Olympia or what was the name? That was, I think that was the Olympia. Bab Frank was leading the band. But Freddie Kepler was the main man. And they supposed to have a guitar player in the band. It was the greatest that we ever was in the Orleans. And I forget his name now. He was a dog, brown skin. All them boys lived down in Frenchwater town, see.
And it was Bud Scott, was it?
No, it wasn't Bud Scott, no. Bud Scott, no. Bud Scott wasn't John. He was this older man than Bud Scott.
Yeah, he was an old fellow. Very sensible fellow. Great man. Can't think of his name. Wasn't Brock? No. What?
Brock Mumford. Brock Mumford. He played with Bolton and Frankie Dewson. I don't know those guitar players.
